Capital One.

Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, Eincorova Coleman, inflation heated up last month, partly
as a result of surging energy prices.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports on the latest cost of living update from the Labor Department.
Consumer prices in September were up 3.7 percent from a year ago.
That's a bigger annual increase than the previous month.
Prices jumped 0.6 percent between August and September, with a spike in gasoline prices
tied to the U.S. war with Iran, accounting for more than half that monthly increase.
The cost of rent, airfare and clothing was also up last month, while grocery prices were
slightly lower.
Stripping out volatile food and energy costs, core inflation was 2.6 percent for the 12
months ending in September.
That's also higher than the previous month.
The Federal Reserve will weigh the cost of living data when officials meet to discuss
interest rates in two weeks.
Scott Horsley in Pierre News, Washington.
President Trump says Taiwan will buy gas from an Alaska pipeline.
He announced the deal yesterday during a campaign rally in Alaska, where he was supporting Republican
candidates.
Pierre's Franco Ordonez reports.
President Trump took the stage in Wasilla, Alaska, urging supporters to help re-elect
Senator Dan Sullivan and other Republican candidates.
The visit is part of a midterm sprint to pump up support for Republican candidates, many
of whom, like Sullivan, are newly vulnerable.
During the rally, Trump announced that Taiwan had agreed to purchase 30 percent of gas from
the Alaska pipeline over the next 20 years, and he said Sullivan was key to the deal.
And I have to say that Dan Sullivan helped me get this done.
Thank you, Dan.
The specific terms of the deal are not clear, but Trump says Taiwan would invest more than
four billion dollars in the project.
Franco Ordonez in Pierre News.
A federal judge has ruled President Trump cannot ban news organizations from the White
House because he doesn't like their coverage.
The media outlets CNN, MS Now and Politico sued after Trump banned more than 70 journalists
from these companies.
The Vatican says Pope Leo had a restful night in the hospital.
He had part of his lower right lung removed during surgery yesterday.
NPR's Scott Detro says Leo's doctors removed it after discovering cancer.
We talked to several lung experts who say that from what the Vatican has said, they're
actually optimistic.
Dr. Vin Gupta from the University of Washington says that the course of action that doctors
took does suggest that they did catch it early and that the cancer has not spread.
And so the fact that surgery was the first tool that they utilized is a really good sign.
He says that if doctors monitor Leo regularly, there is a chance this really wouldn't affect
his lifespan at all.
Many people live without two full lungs, and one person who lived decades without them was
actually Pope Francis.
He had part of a lung removed at a young age.
NPR's Scott Detro reporting.
This is NPR.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is going to meet new British Prime Minister Andy
Burnham today in London.
This comes as Russia steps up its attacks on Ukraine.
Zelensky tells NPR the White House threatened to cut off intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
He says the Trump administration is demanding that Ukraine stop firing long-range drones
and Russian oil refineries.
And Trump claims that Ukraine is driving up the costs of diesel for consumers.
Zelensky says that, in fact, the U.S. war against Iran is doing that.
The WNBA has announced that games three and four of next week's finals will be rescheduled.
NPR's Becky Sullivan reports the change was needed to accommodate conflicts at Atlanta's
major arena.
The Atlanta Dream have swept their way through the playoffs to reach the WNBA Finals for
the first time in 13 years, where they'll face the Golden State Valkyries.
There was just one problem.
The Dream normally play in a very small arena.
The Gateway Center arena was built before the league's boom in popularity, and it seats
just 3,500 fans, far too few for the very biggest games of the WNBA season.
Often the Dream moves marquee games to State Farm Arena, home of the NBA team, the Atlanta
Hawks, but there were scheduling conflicts with games three and four, concert one night
in the Hawks home opener and the other, a situation critics called embarrassing and
avoidable.
Now, the league says game three will be moved up a night, while game four will tip off a
few hours early in the Hawks game a little later that night to fit both.
Becky Sullivan, NPR News.
And I'm Cora Vekulman, NPR News, from Washington.
